mechanism_narrative: A steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 13.6 to 9.9 over four weeks) indicates people are leaving home more often, which mechanically increases foot traffic to retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent rise in TRANSIT mobility (from -47.6 to -39.0 over four weeks) reflects growing use of public transport for commuting and leisure, which correlates with increased retail and recreation activity, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to rise over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC falls below its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility falls below -20 percent, it signals renewed remote-work mandates or restrictions that suppress weekday retail footfall, causing RETAIL_REC to decline over the following four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES falls below -20 but RETAIL_REC increases relative to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility, both trending upward, indicates a broad return to pre-pandemic routines; this combined signal amplifies retail and recreation footfall, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: During an early reopening phase, improvements in TRANSIT mobility are the primary driver of retail recovery, as they enable more trips to retail venues; RESIDENTIAL decline reinforces this effect, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If in an early reopening phase, TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL declines, but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility near zero indicates that consumers are not stockpiling essentials, freeing up discretionary spending and trips for retail and recreation, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±2 percent of baseline for four weeks but RETAIL_REC declines relative to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in PARKS mobility above -10 percent signals the onset of spring weather, which increases outdoor leisure activity and spills over into nearby retail and recreation venues, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises above -10 but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility combined with a simultaneous drop in RETAIL_REC indicates a broad pullback in out-of-home activity, likely due to adverse weather or restrictions, which predicts further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC falls week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC falls week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC increases over the next week relative to its last 28-day mean.
